newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian cenbank further trims reserve requirement.
newsitem.headline: Croatian cenbank further trims reserve requirement.

text.p: Croatia's central bank said on Thursday it had trimmed October reserve requirement for banks by 1.1 points after leaving it unchanged in September.
"(The cut) is modest but represents only one in a series of measures," vice governor Relja Martic told a news conference.
He said the latest cut brought the reserve ratio down to 35.85 percent of kuna deposits from 41 percent at the beginning of 1996.
The bank might consider further relaxation of its policy and slowly abandon prohibitive measures to allow the banking sector more breathing space.
Although the situation called for no drastic cuts in statutory reserves for some time, Martic said commercial banks had improved the regulation of their money flows.
More of them were channelling excess liquidity into government securities, central bank bills and treasury bills, to prevent it from spilling into unbridled consumption or bad loans.

"We find we can almost entirely rely on market instruments," Martic said, adding that the bank would keep a close eye on all monetary developments nevertheless. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
